description.value: The Gorge & Tillicum BC Liquor Store is a government-operated retail outlet — one of 198 BCLIQUOR stores across British Columbia run by the provincial Liquor Distribution Branch. It sells wine, beer, spirits, coolers, ciders, and non-alcoholic beverages. A touring cyclist passing through Victoria's Gorge–Tillicum neighbourhood might stop here to purchase packaged beverages for the road.

bike_parking_detail: 3 racks within 100m: stands (3 spaces, covered) at 40m; stands (2 spaces) at 44m; rack (5 spaces, covered) at 91m. Total: 10 spaces.

raw_osm.name: BC Liquor Store
raw_osm.note: Open regular hours most public holidays.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies this as a BC Liquor Store (shop=alcohol) at 2955 Tillicum Road, Victoria. The website confirms the location exists and is branded as the 'GORGE & TILLICUM' store, creating a name mismatch with OSM. The website content is entirely a product catalogue and corporate information page with no mention of bike parking, washrooms, water access, or any cyclist-relevant amenity, leaving all required and optional criteria unverifiable.
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM records this as 'BC Liquor Store' but the website identifies the location as 'GORGE & TILLICUM'.
No phone number present in OSM record or on the store-specific website page.
OSM address lacks city, province, and postal code.
Category 'Food & Drink' is a poor fit for a retail-only alcohol shop with no prepared food or drink service.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a large government-run retail alcohol chain with no confirmed cyclist amenities and no evidence of bike parking, washrooms, or water access. A packaged-goods retail store does not meaningfully serve touring cyclists as a Food & Drink destination and provides no value to WWC directory users beyond what any grocery or convenience store would.

provenance.category_correction_reason: This is a retail alcohol shop (shop=alcohol), not a food or drink establishment in the cycling tourism sense. 'Retail' would be more appropriate, but no alternative category is available in the provided list.
